original_value: A disruptive technology often used in finance, Internet of Things (IoT) and healthcare, blockchain can reach consensus within a decentralised network—potentially composed of large amounts of unreliable nodes—and to permanently and irreversibly store data in a tamper-proof manner. In this paper, we present a reputation system for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). It considers the users interested in traffic information as the main actors of the architecture. They securely share their data which are collectively validated by other users. Users can choose to employ either such crowd-sourced validated data or data generated by the system to travel between two locations. The data saved is reliable, based on the providers’ reputation and cannot be modified. We present results with a simulation for three cities: San Francisco, Rome and Beijing. We have demonstrated the impact of malicious attacks as the average speed decreased if erroneous information was stored in the blockchain as an implemented routing algorithm guides the honest cars on other free routes, and thus crowds other intersections.

result.paraphrase: A disruptive technology widely used in finance, the Internet of Things (IoT), and healthcare, blockchain can achieve consensus in a decentralised network—potentially made up of many unreliable nodes—and store data permanently and irreversibly in a tamper-proof way. In this paper, we introduce a reputation system for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). It treats users seeking traffic information as the architecture’s main actors. They securely share data that other users collectively validate. When traveling between two locations, users may rely either on this crowd-sourced, validated data or on data generated by the system. The stored data is trustworthy, grounded in providers’ reputation, and unchangeable. We present simulation results for three cities: San Francisco, Rome, and Beijing. We show the effect of malicious attacks: the average speed declined when erroneous information was stored in the blockchain, as the implemented routing algorithm directs honest cars onto other free routes, thereby crowding other intersections.
